newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault to meet Europe staff council on June 3.
newsitem.headline: Renault to meet Europe staff council on June 3.

text.p: French carmaker Renault, complying with court rulings criticising the way it announced the closure of the Vilvoorde plant, will meet representatives of its European staff on June 3 to discuss the shutdown.

The European staff committee, in a statement announcing the meeting, said it hoped Renault's management would not treat the occasion as a formality "as the committee has no intention of accepting a meeting gutted of its meaning".
Officials at Renault declined to discuss the agenda for the meeting.
Courts in France and Belgium have ruled that Renault did not properly notify staff in February of plans to close the plant in judgments which do not, however, bear on the closure decision itself.

Earlier this month, a French appeals court ruled that Renault was not required to give the European works committee advance notice, but it agreed with a lower court that Renault could not close the plant before convening the committee to discuss the reasons and the impact.

Renault has said it needs to close the plant as part of a plan to streamline its money-losing European operations. Vilvoorde is not the mother plant for any new models and its production can easily be shifted to other plants.
Renault initially said the plant was to be closed by the end of July but has since said the deadline could be extended by a few weeks or months.

The company has said the rulings will not affect the timetable but union representatives say they hope to delay the closure using procedural tactics. The European staff committee will hold a news conference in Paris on Wednesday.
